title: research-agent-tests: an audit of agent instruction files in research software and a 19-bug pilot on agent-written regression tests
description:
Evidence for one question: when a coding agent fixes a bug in research software and also writes the regression test, does the test prove anything, or does it share the fix's misunderstanding?

audit/: 38 widely used research software repositories checked for root-level agent instruction files (20 have one); all 20 files read in full and tabulated by what they say about tests.

pilot/: 19 real wrong-result bugs from 9 projects (networkx, pint, xarray, mne-python, numpyro, ESMValCore, statsmodels, nilearn, pyvista) and 73 agent runs in three rounds. In rounds 2 and 3 the agent wrote both the fix and the test. Round 3 (55 runs, protocol committed before the first run): in 12 runs the agent's fix failed the maintainers' tests while the agent's own test passed on it; read by hand, 5 of these leave wrong results, 3 fix less than the maintainers did, and 4 are defensible choices that the reference tests rule out. 7 of 9 repeated runs gave the same verdicts. Grading is mechanical; the hand reading is labelled as such. Scripts, protocol, agent-written tests, diffs, verdicts and token use are included.

These are pilot numbers for a larger study design, not results. See README.md for how to reproduce and for the limits.
